To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the spin-orbit coupling and the exchange field induce spontaneous spin and electric currents in a superconductor- ferromagnet heterostructure.

in an isotropic superconductor deposited on a ferromagnet with a large spin-orbit coupling the spontaneous surface currents arise due to the joint effect of the exchange field and spin-orbit interaction, and the spin current is generated by a different velocity of electron and hole components of Andreev surface state, while electric surface current is generated by an asymmetry of Andeev states with respect of sign reversal of the component of momentum parallel to the surface.
spin-orbit interaction in ferromagnet induces spontaneous spin and electric currents in superconductor, which are carried by Andeev states and are present at all temperatures below superconductor Tc.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of the spin-orbital coupling on the proximity-induced spin currents and electric currents in superconductor/ferromagnet heterojunctions.
the effects of spin-orbit coupling on the superconducting state of a ferromagnetic superconductor (F/S) heterostructure.
the effect of the spin orbit interaction on a superconductor- ferromagnet (S-F) hybrid structure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the spin-orbit effect in ferromagnetic layers leads to a significant modification of the superconducting state of the whole heterostructure.

spin-orbit interaction in the ferromagnet is necessary to generate the spin current, while the electric current may be induced in the supercon-ductor even in the absence of the ferromagnet with spin-orbit coupling.
the proximity induced electric and spin currents in a ferromagnetic-superconductor heterostructure are not necessarily related to each other and can be generated independently.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the spin-orbit coupling can generate a spin and electric currents in a superconducting film with ferromagnetic layer, which are independent of the exchange field.
spin-orbit interaction is crucial for the generation of the electric and spin surface current.

the spin-orbit coupling in the ferromagnet is a necessary ingredient for generating both the electric and spin surface current, while the electric current can be generated in a superconductor without spin-orbit interaction, but the spin surface current is not possible in this case.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proximity effect can be used to create and manipulate spin and electric currents in superconducting systems with a thin magnetic layer.

spin-orbit interaction in the ferromagnetic layer can lead to the emergence of the spontaneous spin and electric currents at the interface between the ferromagnet and a conventional s-wave superconduc-tor.
a spontaneous spin current in a superconductor is not a unique signature of spin-triplet superconductivity, as it is often assumed.
